brief.pitch: You know your pond: sling past visitors on fast ice and bank off bumpers.

aspects.title: Fast and slow
aspects.line: Hit orange ice to zoom. Blue slush drags you down.
aspects.detail: Two fast_ice rects (strength 0.6, about +30%) and two slow_ice circles (strength 0.7, about -35%), point-symmetric, painted by rink_toys.gd. Zones also change the puck. Positions never move, so knowledge pays.

alternatives.title: Late thaw
alternatives.line: A bigger slush field turns the middle into a swamp.

alternatives.title: One highway
alternatives.line: One long fast strip down the middle everybody fights over.

aspects.title: Corner bumpers
aspects.line: Smack the corner post and the puck flies back faster.
aspects.detail: Four rink.obstacles of kind bumper, size 2.5 m, at x ±26, z ±11. The core returns the puck at restitution 1.6. Round faces make the exit angle depend on the contact point, so aim is a skill.

alternatives.title: Bouncy patches
alternatives.line: Painted bumper circles throw the puck from their edges.

alternatives.title: Centre posts
alternatives.line: Bumpers stand mid-pond, splitting every rush in two.

aspects.title: Skate, pass, steal
aspects.line: Sprint past, pass across, poke it back, or bump them.
aspects.detail: The core's sprint, shot, lead pass, poke and body check, unchanged. Reception radius 2.5 m makes cross-crease passes catchable; a shot inside the core's one-timer window beats a crease skater caught moving across.

alternatives.title: No hitting
alternatives.line: Checks off: only pokes and passes win the puck.

alternatives.title: Bruiser pond
alternatives.line: Heavier bodies fall easily, so every rush risks a crash.

aspects.title: City visitors
aspects.line: Beginners chase you straight. Better ones arrive sooner and shoot sharper.
aspects.detail: Core bots at rookie by default, body_check 0.3. Chaser hunts the carrier, supports offer lanes, back guards the crease. Check wind-up 12 frames. HOME's level row raises them to pro or all_star.

alternatives.title: Outnumbered local
alternatives.line: Three locals face five visitors and must use the ice.

alternatives.title: Sharp visitors
alternatives.line: Pro bots from the first drop, no warm-up.

aspects.title: First to five
aspects.line: Five goals win. Fall two behind and your team speeds up.
aspects.detail: rules.score_to_win 5. An on_goal hook at a lead of two gives the conceding side 600 frames of 1.15x speed and announces it, for either team. About three to four minutes; R rematches.

alternatives.title: Beat the dusk
alternatives.line: A three-minute clock; most goals before dark wins.

alternatives.title: Golden goal
alternatives.line: One goal ends it, so every bank matters.

aspects.title: Over your shoulder
aspects.line: See the next orange patch before you reach it.
aspects.detail: Core chase camera unchanged: 6 m behind, 3.5 m high, 5 m look-ahead, 4 frames lag, radar on. Daylight tier l1_day keeps orange and blue patches distinct. Greybox checks patch readability from play height.

alternatives.title: Higher view
alternatives.line: A raised camera shows more patches, with smaller skaters.

alternatives.title: Whole pond
alternatives.line: A fixed arena view shows every lane at once.

brief.rules:
FANTASY: I own this pond: I know every fast run, slush patch and bumper, and visitors cannot keep up. Fantasy and challenge.
WORLD: Skater 1.8 m tall, 0.8 m body width; pond 75 body widths long, 37 body widths wide; top speed 6 body heights a second, 8 on fast ice; camera 3 body heights behind, 2 up.
TEARDOWN: Mario Kart 8: cross a dash panel for a burst, off-road slows you; copied without a button as orange fast ice (+30% speed) and blue slush (-35%).
TEARDOWN: NHL '94: pass across the crease, shoot as it arrives, the goalie cannot cross in time; copied with the core's lead pass and one-timer shot.
TEARDOWN: Rocket League: six boost pads sit in fixed places and veterans win the race there; changed to four ice patches that never move.
30 SECONDS: 0-5 s: puck drops, orange runs show, you move: "my pond". 5-15 s: skate onto orange and pull away from a clumsy chaser: "they can't catch me". 15-30 s: fire off a corner bumper toward a mate or net, risking a turnover: "I banked that".
KILL IF: after one match a newcomer never steers toward orange or around blue, or cannot say what either patch did.
KILL IF: the carrier crossing a fast run feels no burst and is caught as often as on plain ice.
KILL IF: after ten tries a player cannot predict a bumper bank, or nobody aims at a bumper again.
KILL IF: after three rounds a newcomer cannot say why they lost the puck.
CARTRIDGE: game.rink.length_m = 60 (small pond, quick rushes)
CARTRIDGE: game.rink.width_m = 30 (two lanes plus a middle)
CARTRIDGE: game.rink.corner_radius_m = 3 (tight corners around the bumpers)
CARTRIDGE: game.rink.board_restitution = 0.6 (lively banks)
CARTRIDGE: game.rink.zones = [{id north-run, rect, x 6, z -9.5, w 22, d 5, fast_ice, 0.6}, {id south-run, rect, x -6, z 9.5, w 22, d 5, fast_ice, 0.6}, {id east-slush, circle, x 11, z 3, r 3.5, slow_ice, 0.7}, {id west-slush, circle, x -11, z -3, r 3.5, slow_ice, 0.7}] (choose your line)
CARTRIDGE: game.rink.obstacles = bumper size 2.5 at [26,11], [26,-11], [-26,11], [-26,-11] (corners kick the puck out)
CARTRIDGE: game.teams = 4 v 4; locals #E8742C... jersey #2E7D4F: player, chaser, support, back; visitors #7A3FA0: chaser, support, support, back; regular spawns scaled to 60 x 30 (room to pass)
CARTRIDGE: game.rules.score_to_win = 5 (a match with swings)
CARTRIDGE: game.effects = [{id dig-in, kind speed, target own_team, duration_frames 600, trigger director, stats skater_speed multiply 1.15}] (the comeback legs)
CARTRIDGE: game.rules.hooks = [{id dig-in, on_goal, team scoring, score lead_at_least 2, then apply_modifier dig-in to conceding 600 frames, announce "DIG IN!"}] (trailing side surges visibly)
CARTRIDGE: game.ai.difficulty = "rookie" (clumsy, never absent)
CARTRIDGE: game.ai.body_check = 0.3 (visitors sometimes hit)
CARTRIDGE: game.stick.reception_m = 2.5 (banked and crease passes get caught)
CARTRIDGE: game.contact.bot_check_windup_frames = 12 (longest readable hit tell)
CARTRIDGE: game.look.tier = "l1_day" (bright pond, readable patches)
SKIN: title = Pond Local
SKIN: tagline = Orange is fast. Blue is slow. Bank the corners.
SKIN: team_names = Pond Locals, City Visitors
SKIN: level words = Weekenders, Day Trippers, Ringers

ROUND: one continuous match, first to 5; core faceoff after each goal; R rematches within 2 s. Colour orders: locals wear green and visitors purple, so jerseys never match the ice; use only #2E7D4F and #7A3FA0 as team colours.
VERBS (frames at 60 Hz): sprint held; shot 4/1/24; pass 4/1/20; poke 0/8/20; check 6/12/30. Only the 24-frame shot cooldown and 12-frame human check window are documented; the rest are estimates the drill harness measures first. The core's values stay.
SPEEDS: 11 m/s base, about 14.3 on fast ice, about 7.2 in slush; accel 12 m/s^2; turn 5 rad/s; carrier 0.92 of base. Zone strengths, bumper size and positions live in the cartridge, the tuning file here; edit between plays.
CONTACT: core momentum law. Bump: both keep control. Stumble: victim loses half speed and maybe the puck; checker loses speed. Knockdown only for hard hits. Missed poke costs the core's recovery or stumble.
INTENSITY: calm faceoff, rush, turnover, goal pause; the dig-in surge makes a second peak; 4-4 is natural sudden death; end card releases.
END: base end card with score and R rematch. "Why" detail is only what the base shows; the person checks it.
COMEBACK: DIG IN is a visible rule for both teams, not hidden help.
DEVIATIONS for the owner: the core caps bot check wind-up at 12 frames, below the 20-frame bar; the skating approach is the longer read. Visitors share the skater body and differ by role and kit, since new figures are rig work. No rule answers a bot figure.
VERIFY: run check-cartridge; confirm bumpers, zone effects on puck and bots, hook and effect behaviour. Bots are not promised to read zones.
brief.arena: Frozen pond rink 60 x 30 m, corner radius 3 m, goals 4 m wide at each end, boards restitution 0.6. Orange fast runs 22 x 5 m: one centred (6, -9.5), one (-6, 9.5). Blue slush circles radius 3.5 m at (11, 3) and (-11, -3), guarding the straight route. Round bumpers 2.5 m wide at (±26, ±11). Layout is point-symmetric, fair to both ends, and never changes during a match. The barn around it stays the base's hall. Camera: core chase view, 6 m behind and 3.5 m up, clamped inside the boards and lifting when crowded, so scenery never sits between lens and skater.
brief.ai: City Visitors, purple kits, thirdjam bots on the skater body. Chaser: heads for the puck carrier; read the approach, turn onto orange and leave them behind; its check winds up 12 frames. Two supports: drift into passing lanes; poke or cut the lane. Back: guards the crease and can be pulled across by a deke or cross-crease pass. Hits change both bodies by the core's momentum law; goals bring the core's pause, horn and commentary. Locals (your mates) use chaser, support and back roles. Levels: rookie reacts slowly and shoots wide; pro and all_star react sooner, shoot sharper and check harder to dodge. No idle bots and no speed cheating; DIG IN applies equally to either team.
brief.controls: move: WASD, skate. aim: mouse, point the stick. primary: left mouse, shoot with puck, defensive stick action without. secondary: right mouse or E, pass with puck, check without. sprint: core sprint key, stamina burst. restart: R after the end card. The core's bindings stay; if they differ, the base HUD's wording wins.
brief.mood: Bright winter afternoon on a village pond: pale ice, loud orange fast runs, cold blue slush, magenta rubber bumpers, green locals against purple visitors; skate hiss, core horn and friendly pond-side commentary.

pillars.line: Pond knowledge wins: choosing your line over the ice is the sharpest weapon.
Every corner is a trick: banks are aimed, learned and risky.
pillars.rules_out: Bonus points or auto-guided bank shots.

pillars.line: Quick readable exchanges where mates, rivals and puck answer each other.

verbs.input: Hold sprint; stack the core stamina burst with orange ice to slingshot past a chaser.
verbs.cancel: Release any time; shot or pass allowed; empty stamina bar ends it.

verbs.input: Primary with puck: tap flat, hold to charge; aim at net or bumper; core skater shot animation.
verbs.cancel: Losing the puck kills the charge; one-timer allowed inside the core's reception window.

verbs.input: Secondary or E with puck: core lead pass toward the aimed mate; core skater pass animation.
verbs.cancel: Receiver may shoot on arrival; opponents intercept with the blade or block with body.

verbs.input: Without puck: core poke takes the puck in reach; body shielding and fresh-possession grace beat it.
verbs.cancel: A miss costs the core's recovery; no cancel.

verbs.input: Without puck: core body check; momentum decides bump, stumble or knockdown for the target.
verbs.cancel: Committed once pressed; carrier cannot check; a whiff loses position.

playstyles.title: Lane runner
playstyles.line: Ride fast ice wide, sprint behind defenders, then cut to the crease.

playstyles.title: Bumper banker
playstyles.line: Skip passes and shots off corners around crowded lanes.

playstyles.title: Slush trapper
playstyles.line: Steer carriers into blue ice, then poke or check them there.

loops.s3: Pick a line: orange speed, short slush shortcut, pass or bank; players learn to bend routes.
loops.s30: Win puck, break out on a run, create a crease pass or bank; overcommitting invites counters.
loops.m3: Race to five, learn the visitors and patches, answer DIG IN surges, then rematch with better lines.

context: Which side holds the puck relative to its nearer fast run.
DIG IN speed surge for a team two goals behind.
Sprint stamina decides who wins the next race.
Score at 4-4 makes the next goal decide everything.

skill.floor: Move and press one button: skate onto orange, then shoot toward the net.
ceiling: Slingshot: enter a fast run already sprinting, exit toward the crease.
Corner bank: choose the bumper contact point that finds a cutting mate.
Slush trap: force a carrier through blue, then poke as they slow.

feel.knockback: Core momentum law: closing speed and mass against stability; boards add to hits; bodies push apart.
feel.reaction: Both change: bump rebounds; hit victim stumbles or falls while checker loses speed; poke takes puck or leaves poker recovering.
feel.whiff: Missed poke or check plays full recovery, loses position, no burst; the carrier skates away.
feel.shake: Keep the base's presentation; any shake only on knockdowns and goals, never taps or whiffs.
feel.camera: Core chase: 6 m behind, 3.5 m up, look-ahead 5 m, lag 4 frames, FOV 70, radar on.

clips.moment: Local sprints across orange ice and bursts clear of a purple chaser.
Puck cracks off a corner bumper to a mate who finishes.
Visitor bogs down in blue slush and loses the puck to a poke.

design.first_minute: Play now, puck drops. One hint: orange fast, blue slow, bank corners. Rookie visitors chase clumsily; sprint, pass and bank immediately.
design.fail_state: End card shows final score and R rematches; the player should recall the lost race, blocked pass or bad line.
out_of_scope: New simulation, skater, camera or verbs.
